facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge
fluctuating lower abdominal pain
fever
progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years, worsening in the last 5 years
difficulty with defecation and voiding
a smooth, firm pelvic mass was palpated extending to two fingers below the umbilicus, with limited mobility
the cervix could not be visualized or sondaged
elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level of 115.6 g/dL
a 269 × 529 mm hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity
a separate 126 × 106 mm homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa with a clear border
a 145 × 110 × 146 mm multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components
no lymphadenopathy was noted

concepts.why: The large hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity and the multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components are suggestive of a malignant uterine tumor, and the elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level supports this diagnosis.
The smooth, firm pelvic mass and the separate homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa are consistent with uterine fibroids, which are common in women of this age group.

The brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fever, and hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity are suggestive of an infected hematometra, which is a possible complication of uterine fibroids or other uterine abnormalities.
The separate homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa could also represent an ovarian fibroma, which is a rare but possible diagnosis in this case.
The elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level and the large hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity are also suggestive of uterine adenocarcinoma, which is a possible diagnosis in this case.
